Breakfast. Spend the day exploring Cusco at your own pace. You can stroll through the old streets, visit museums, shop for souvenirs or take a break at a café.

Two optional excursions are available if you'd like to venture outside the city.

A full-day trip to the Sacred Valley costs $220 per person.

In Pisac, visit a craft market selling ceramics and goods made from wool, silver and leather. At Awanakancha, see llamas, alpacas, guanacos and vicuñas and learn how wool is processed and coloured with natural dyes.

At Ollantaytambo, explore the archaeological complex, with its monumental terraces, stone buildings and remains of fortifications. Views of the Andean valleys open up between stops, and the trip takes in both Inca heritage and local crafts.

Lunch is a buffet at a restaurant serving Peruvian cuisine. Return to Cusco for the night at the 4-star Xima Cusco or a comparable hotel.

The trip to Vinicunca Rainbow Mountain takes a full day. A group tour with an English-speaking guide costs $55 per person. A private tour with an English-speaking guide costs $200 per person for groups of two or more.

Layers of minerals create the coloured bands on the slopes, where red, yellow, green and white rocks lie side by side. Vinicunca is about 100 km from Cusco in Quispicanchi Province. The route reaches around 5,200 m, and the mountain offers views of nearby ranges and Ausangate, a peak sacred to the Incas.

Leave at around 04:00 and return to Cusco at about 19:00. Breakfast and lunch are included. Good physical endurance is needed at this altitude. You can ride a horse for part of the ascent if you wish. Horse hire costs $40.

Overnight at the 4-star Xima Cusco or a comparable hotel.
